pricing_terms: Term SOFR loans bear Term SOFR, subject to a 0.50% floor, plus 3.25% per annum; revolving SOFR loans bear the same benchmark and floor plus 3.00%. Base-rate margins are 2.25% for term loans and 2.00% for revolving loans. Interest is payable quarterly in arrears and at period end, using a 360-day year for SOFR interest. The unused revolving commitment fee is 0.375% per annum, payable quarterly. Letter-of-credit fees are charged at the revolving margin. A 1.00% repricing premium applies to term loans repriced within six months after closing.
agreement_text: CREDIT AGREEMENT dated January 15, 2025, among Alder Ridge Components, LLC, as Borrower, the domestic subsidiaries identified as Guarantors, the lenders from time to time party hereto, and Meridian Commercial Bank, as Administrative Agent. 1. Facilities. Subject to the conditions herein, the Lenders make a $180,000,000 USD term facility and a $40,000,000 USD revolving facility available. The term loans are funded in full on the Closing Date. Revolving borrowings may be made, repaid and reborrowed until the Revolving Commitment Termination Date, subject to a $5,000,000 minimum borrowing and $1,000,000 increments. Letters of credit and swingline loans count against revolving availability, with sublimits of $8,000,000 and $5,000,000, respectively. Proceeds may refinance existing indebtedness, pay transaction expenses, fund working capital and general corporate purposes, and finance permitted acquisitions. Each borrowing request is irrevocable and must specify the amount, type and interest period. 2. Interest and Fees. Term SOFR loans bear interest at Term SOFR for the elected one-, three- or six-month period, subject to a 0.50% floor, plus 3.25% per annum; revolving SOFR loans bear the same benchmark and floor plus 3.00%. Base-rate loans bear the applicable base rate plus 2.25% for term loans or 2.00% for revolving loans. Interest is payable quarterly in arrears and at each period end; SOFR interest uses a 360-day year. The Borrower pays a 0.375% annual commitment fee on the daily unused revolving commitments, quarterly in arrears, and customary letter-of-credit fees at the revolving margin. 3. Maturity and Prepayment. The term loans and revolving commitments mature January 15, 2030. Term loans amortize quarterly at an annual rate of 1.00% of original principal, with the balance due at maturity. Revolving loans are due at maturity. Voluntary prepayments are permitted without premium, subject to accrued interest and three business days' notice for SOFR loans. A 1.00% premium applies to a repricing transaction involving term loans completed within six months after closing. The Borrower must prepay term loans with 100% of net cash proceeds of non-permitted debt and, subject to reinvestment within 12 months, asset-sale or casualty proceeds exceeding $10,000,000 in any fiscal year. Annual excess-cash-flow prepayments are 50% when year-end net leverage exceeds 3.50:1.00, 25% when it is at or below 3.50:1.00 but above 3.00:1.00, and zero at or below 3.00:1.00. 4. Financial Covenant. If revolving loans, swingline loans and unreimbursed letter-of-credit drawings exceed 35% of revolving commitments on the last day of a fiscal quarter, the Borrower must maintain a consolidated net leverage ratio no greater than 5.50:1.00. Testing occurs quarterly while that condition is met. Equity contributions may cure a breach within 10 business days after delivery of the relevant compliance certificate, subject to no more than two cures in any four-quarter period and no consecutive-quarter cures. 5. Negative Covenants. Until obligations are paid and commitments terminated, the Borrower and restricted subsidiaries may not incur debt, create liens, make investments or restricted payments, sell assets, merge, or transact with affiliates except as permitted. Exceptions include ordinary-course trade payables; purchase-money debt and liens capped at $15,000,000 outstanding; investments in subsidiaries and ordinary-course employee advances; annual restricted payments of $10,000,000 plus retained excess cash flow; asset sales for fair value with at least 75% cash consideration; and mergers where the Borrower survives. Affiliate transactions must be on arm's-length terms, except for permitted compensation and intercompany transactions. 6. Waiver. By a written amendment dated October 15, 2025, the Administrative Agent and Required Lenders waived the financial-covenant default arising solely from the Borrower's 5.62:1.00 net leverage ratio for the fiscal quarter ended June 30, 2025. The waiver applies only to that quarter and does not amend the 5.50:1.00 threshold or waive any other default. Amendments and waivers otherwise require written consent of the Required Lenders, and the consent of each directly affected lender is required for reductions in principal, interest margin or pro rata share, extensions of its payment dates or increases in its commitment. 7. Events of Default and Remedies. Events of default include failure to pay principal when due; failure to pay interest or fees within five business days; breach of specified affirmative or negative covenants; other covenant breaches continuing 30 days after notice; materially incorrect representations; cross-default to other debt of at least $20,000,000 after applicable grace periods; bankruptcy or insolvency; final judgments exceeding $15,000,000 not discharged, bonded or stayed within 60 days; and invalidity of a material loan document or guarantee. Upon a continuing event of default, the Agent may, and at the direction of Required Lenders shall, terminate commitments, accelerate amounts owing and exercise secured-party remedies, subject to applicable law. 8. Information and Protection. The Borrower must deliver quarterly and annual financial statements, annual budgets, compliance certificates and prompt written notice of defaults and material litigation. The Borrower must pay documented reasonable out-of-pocket Agent and lender expenses and indemnify them for specified transaction-related claims, subject to customary exclusions for a recipient's gross negligence, bad faith or willful misconduct. The Agent may rely on notices and certificates reasonably believed genuine.
events_of_default: Defaults include principal nonpayment when due; interest or fee nonpayment continuing five business days; specified covenant breaches; other covenant breaches continuing 30 days after notice; materially incorrect representations; cross-default on at least $20,000,000 of other debt after applicable grace periods; bankruptcy or insolvency; unsatisfied or unstayed final judgments above $15,000,000 for 60 days; and invalidity of a material loan document or guarantee. During a continuing default, the Agent may or, when directed by Required Lenders, shall terminate commitments, accelerate the debt and exercise secured-party remedies, subject to applicable law.
financial_covenants: A springing consolidated net leverage covenant applies if revolving loans, swingline loans and unreimbursed letter-of-credit drawings exceed 35% of revolving commitments at quarter end. While triggered, the maximum ratio is 5.50:1.00 and is tested quarterly. The Borrower may cure a breach with an equity contribution within 10 business days after delivery of the compliance certificate, but may not use more than two cures in any four-quarter period or cure in consecutive quarters.
loan_facility_terms: The facilities are a $180,000,000 USD term loan funded in full at closing and a $40,000,000 USD revolving facility available for borrowing, repayment and reborrowing until its termination date. The revolving facility includes $8,000,000 for letters of credit and $5,000,000 for swingline loans, both counting toward availability. Minimum revolving borrowings are $5,000,000, in $1,000,000 increments. Permitted uses include refinancing, transaction expenses, working capital, general corporate purposes and permitted acquisitions.
professional_summary: The agreement provides Alder Ridge Components with a $180 million term loan and a $40 million revolving facility, maturing January 15, 2030. Pricing is floating-rate with stated SOFR floors and margins, plus commitment and letter-of-credit fees. Term debt amortizes at 1% annually, with specified mandatory prepayments and leverage-based excess-cash-flow sweeps. A springing quarterly net-leverage test applies when revolving exposure exceeds 35% of commitments; a one-quarter waiver for the June 2025 test did not change the ongoing threshold. Negative covenants contain enumerated baskets. Specified payment, covenant, cross-default, insolvency, judgment and document-validity events can permit acceleration and enforcement. Reporting, expense-reimbursement and indemnity obligations protect the lenders.
restrictive_covenants: The Borrower and restricted subsidiaries are restricted from incurring debt, granting liens, making investments or restricted payments, selling assets, merging and entering affiliate transactions, subject to stated exceptions. These include purchase-money debt and liens up to $15,000,000 outstanding; a $10,000,000 annual restricted-payment basket plus retained excess cash flow; fair-value asset sales with at least 75% cash consideration; specified subsidiary investments and employee advances; and mergers in which the Borrower survives. Affiliate transactions generally must be on arm's-length terms, subject to stated exceptions.
waivers_and_amendments: An October 15, 2025 written amendment by the Administrative Agent and Required Lenders waived only the financial-covenant default caused by the 5.62:1.00 ratio for the quarter ended June 30, 2025. It did not change the 5.50:1.00 covenant or waive another default. Other amendments and waivers generally require Required Lender consent. Each directly affected lender must consent to specified changes to principal, margin, pro rata sharing, payment dates or its commitment.
maturity_and_repayment_terms: Both facilities mature January 15, 2030. Term loans amortize quarterly at an annual rate of 1.00% of original principal, with remaining principal due at maturity; revolving loans are due at maturity. Voluntary prepayment is permitted without premium, subject to accrued interest and three business days' notice for SOFR loans. Mandatory term-loan prepayments include 100% of net cash proceeds from non-permitted debt and qualifying asset-sale or casualty proceeds above $10,000,000 per fiscal year, subject to a 12-month reinvestment period. Excess-cash-flow sweeps are 50% above 3.50:1.00 net leverage, 25% at or below 3.50:1.00 but above 3.00:1.00, and zero at or below 3.00:1.00.
lender_rights_and_borrower_obligations: The Borrower must provide quarterly and annual financial statements, annual budgets, compliance certificates and prompt notice of defaults and material litigation. It must pay documented reasonable out-of-pocket Agent and lender expenses and provide the stated indemnity, subject to exclusions for a recipient's gross negligence, bad faith or willful misconduct. The Agent may rely on notices and certificates reasonably believed genuine. The Agent and Required Lenders hold the stated waiver, amendment, acceleration and enforcement rights, with individual affected-lender consent protected for specified fundamental changes.
